1. The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.2,36,244/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred is not in dispute.
The B.M.T.C. by not filing an appeal has accepted its liability to pay the compensation.
3. The Tribunal has taken the view that the claimant would not be entitled to any loss of future income since it was stated that the claimant continued working in the garment factory.
4. Learned counsel for the claimant contends that the observation of Tribunal is incorrect, since the claimant had categorically stated that at present he was not working.
5. It is to be stated here that when the claimant has suffered a fracture of tibia and fibula, there would necessarily be a loss of earning capacity.
In this case the treated Doctor was not examined and the Doctor who assessed the disability stated that the claimant had suffered the disability at 22% to the whole body.
In my view, it would be appropriate to assess the disability at 10% to the whole body.
6. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.9,000/- to award compensation under the head 'loss of income during laid-up period.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2018, would be Rs.12,500/-.
7. As the claimant was aged 38 years, a multiplier of '15' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,25,000/- (Rs.12,500/- x 12 x '15' x 10%) towards 'loss of future income' .
8. As a consequence, the amount of Rs.9,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.25,000/- (Rs.12,500/- X 2 months).
9. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.35,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

10. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities, as against the sum of Rs.20,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

11. Having regard to the length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital, the claimant would also be entitled to 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges' at Rs.20,000/- as against the sum of Rs.1,500/- awarded by the Tribunal.

12. The sums awarded as medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence,
does not call for modification and hence confirmed.

2
13. The sum awarded under the head 'future medical expenses' is just and proper and is affirmed.
The said sum does not carry any interest.
14. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

Sl. Particulars Award by Award by  No. Tribunal this Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)
 1. Loss of future income - 2,25,000/-
 2. Pain and agony 35,000/- 50,000/-
 3. Medical expenses 1,50,744/- 1,50,744/-
 4. Food, attendant, 1,500/- 20,000/-
 conveyance,
 nourishment and  other incidental  charges etc.
 5. Loss of income during 9,000/- 25,000/-
 laid up period  6. Loss of amenities in 20,000/- 50,000/-
 life  7. Future medical 20,000/- 20,000/-
 expenses

15 . Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.5,40,744/- as against Rs.2,36,244/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The B.M.T.C. is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
17. The apportionment of the compensation amount would be interms of the Award of the Tribunal.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
